comments.comment: Pregnancy isn't just a minor inconvenience. It changes nearly every system in the body. It can lead to mood swings, emotional sensitivity, memory problems ("pregnancy brain"), fatigue, and loss of sleep. Hormones play a major role: hCG commonly causes harsh fatigue and, for many women, daily nausea, especially during the first 13–14 weeks. Relaxin widens the pelvis, but also makes joints less stable, increasing back pain and the risk of sprains. The uterus grows from just 60–80 g to around 1 kg, and its volume expands from 10 mL to 5+ liters. This causes pressure on the bladder, intestines, stomach, and diaphragm, while stretching abdominal muscles, sometimes causing diastasis recti. Blood volume increases by up to 50%, making the heart beat 10–20 BPM faster and putting extra strain on women, with increased health risk for women with heart conditions. Blood also clots more easily, increasing the risk of blood clots, while urinary tract infections and gallstones become more common. The average pregnancy adds 11–16 kg of weight. Combined with relaxin and the enlarged uterus shifting the center of gravity, this often causes back, hip, and pelvic pain, increased lower back curvature, balance problems, a waddling gait, and pelvic floor damage that may require rehabilitation. Now childbirth: 20–30% of first births involve prolonged labor, increasing pain, exhaustion, infection risk, C-section risk, and fetal distress. C-sections occur in 20–35% of births and increase bleeding, infection risk, blood clots, recovery time, and leave a permanent scar. Perineal tears occur in 50–90% of first births (abortion is in 40% of cases the womans first pregnancy), with 5–6% being severe, causing intense pain and pelvic floor problems. Postpartum hemorrhage affects 4–5% of births, which is about 1 in 20, and involves severe bleeding. Shoulder dystocia occurs in 0.5–3% of births and can permanently injure the baby while increasing the mother's pain, tearing, and bleeding. Preeclampsia affects 3–8% of pregnancies and can progress to seizures, strokes, placental abruption, and organ failure.
